baseline_note: Current law, 2027–2031, all building sizes, from the shared all-housing baseline (the same for every pairing). It includes a small statewide adjustment not assigned to any place.
double_count: Both reforms make it easier to build apartments near frequent transit. A building that goes ahead because the law allows more height and also because it no longer needs a parking garage would be counted once by each reform's estimate. Adding the two estimates near stops counts it twice. Away from stops only the parking reform acts, so there is nothing to double count and the two are simply added.
rule_c: Rule (c), adding both and then subtracting the overlap measured in cities that did both reforms, is a sensitivity case only and has no number yet. The cities that could measure it differ from Wisconsin and from each other: New York kept its parking minimums near transit, while Charlotte, Chicago and Saint Paul cut them, in different markets and decades.

a.info: Near stops, both reforms' additions are added. If the same new building would be counted by both reforms, it is counted twice, so this is the high reading.
a.label: Rule (a): add both near stops

b.info: Near stops, each place gets whichever reform adds more there in that year, as if the smaller one were already inside the larger. This is the low reading.
b.label: Rule (b): the larger of the two near stops
